passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer’s remains were recovered approximately 1.5 miles from Bowman’s trailer.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Canadian authorities were holding Bowman. He had been encountered in Canada in connection with unrelated matters, including allegations concerning driving while intoxicated and immigration issues.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators in Virginia and North Carolina wanted to question him concerning the Short case. They also sought access to Bowman’s vehicle.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman had not been charged with the Short murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators announced plans to travel to Canada to question Garrison S. Bowman, 60, of Mayodan, North Carolina.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: During Canadian proceedings, authorities described information alleging that Bowman had been involved in a business dispute connected to moving a mobile home.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A Canadian judge ordered Bowman held for an additional seven days.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The court reportedly considered him a flight risk and someone who might pose a danger to the public.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman appeared at a Canadian detention hearing in Yellowknife.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police disclosed that they had known about Bowman earlier but became more interested after Jennifer’s remains were discovered near his home.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police described him as a possible witness, not a suspect.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Their objectives included interviewing Bowman and searching his van.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators planned to travel to Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada, to interview Garrison Bowman and search his van after learning Canadian authorities held him.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Plans to interview Bowman were temporarily delayed while investigators waited for the diplomatic and legal authorization necessary to conduct investigative activity in Canada. The delay concerned how American investigators could legally question Bowman and obtain evidence located inside Canada, not whether investigators intended to travel there.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sheriff Cassell said investigators wanted to learn everything they could about Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Cassell explained that once Jennifer’s remains were discovered near Bowman’s former trailer, authorities realized they needed to examine him again.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman publicly complained that false information had been provided to the FBI and North Carolina authorities.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators continued stressing publicly that Bowman had not been charged with killing the Short family.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Four investigators from the Henry County Sheriff’s Office and Rockingham County Sheriff’s Office traveled to Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada, as part of the investigation into the murders of Michael, Mary and Jennifer Short. Investigators sought to question Garrison Bowman and pursue evidence associated with his van.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The FBI Legal Attaché became involved after learning that local investigators intended to travel to Canada to interview Bowman and search his van, apparently believing that a North Carolina search warrant could be used in Canada. The Legal Attaché attempted to intervene because the search required coordination with Canadian authorities and compliance with Canadian law.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators were in Yellowknife.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Two Rockingham County investigators interviewed Bowman following his Canadian deportation hearing.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The two Henry County investigators did not participate in that interview. Sheriff Frank Cassell said his investigators planned to question Bowman after he returned to the United States.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Canadian authorities continued processing Bowman for deportation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Martinsville Church of God planned visitation and funeral services.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer was buried after approximately six weeks of uncertainty concerning her fate.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer’s Funeral: After DNA identification, authorities made arrangements to return Jennifer’s remains to her family.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Canadian authorities scheduled Bowman for deportation over immigration violations. Investigators postponed an interview until his return to the United States. Jennifer’s funeral was held.
